chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn al-Mughira, from Hariz, from Ibn Abi Yafur, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'A man sees [a dream] in sleep and feels desire, then wakes up and looks but finds nothing. Then he waits afterwards and it comes out.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he is sick, let him perform ghusl; and if he is not sick, there is nothing upon him [no ghusl required].'

He (the narrator) said: 'So I said to him, 'What is the difference between the two?'' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Because when the man is healthy, it comes with a spurt and strength, and when he is sick, it does not come except afterwards [without force/spurt].'
ai.seo_question: When is ghusl required after a dream discharge if no fluid is found immediately upon waking?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between seminal discharge (mani) and pre-seminal fluid (madhi) based on the physical force of ejection, a key criterion in Shia fiqh for determining the necessity of ritual bath (ghusl). The Imam explains that a healthy person's discharge is forceful, requiring ghusl, whereas a sick person's is weak, indicating it is not full mani. This ruling highlights the practical application of physiological signs in determining ritual purity status.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibn Al Mugheira, from Hareyz, from Ibn Abu Yafour who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The man sees (a dream) in the sleep and finds the excitement, but (when) he wakes up and looks, he does not find anything. Then he waits afterwards, so it (discharge) comes out’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If he was sick so let him wash, and if he does not happen to be sick, then there is nothing upon him’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘So what is the difference between the two?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Because the man, when he was healthy, it would come with ejaculation (spurts) and strength, and when he was sick, it would not come except afterwards’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ibn al-Mughirah from Hariz from ibn abu Ya‘fur who has said the following:

“I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, there is a man who experiences wet dream and orgasm. He then wakes up and does not find anything, but after a while discharge takes place. He (the Imam) said, ‘If he suffers from an illness, he must take Ghusl (bath), but if he does not suffer from any illness he is not obligated for Ghusl (bath).’

I then asked him (the Imam), ‘What is the difference between the two cases?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is because in the case of one without illness, it comes spurting and with force, but in the case of one suffering from an illness it comes later.’”
